story_description: Create the foundational data model and types for representing hook execution events in a timeline/Gantt chart format, enabling visualization of hook lifecycles with proper temporal relationships and hierarchical structure.
task_description: Implement the HookTimelineBuilder struct that converts raw HookExecution arrays into hierarchical HookTimelineEvent trees suitable for Gantt visualization, supporting both turn-level and session-level view modes with provider-agnostic event normalization.
atom_description: Implement HookTimelineBuilder struct with static factory methods buildTurnTimeline and buildSessionTimeline that transform HookExecution arrays into HookTimelineEvent hierarchies. Include normalizeEventType method for mapping provider-specific event names (Claude PreToolUse, Gemini tool_call_start, Codex exec_start) to unified HookTimelineCategory enum values. Handle parent-child relationship construction, depth calculation, and time range normalization.
problem_statement: The Gantt visualization requires transforming flat HookExecution arrays from HookStore into hierarchical HookTimelineEvent trees. Raw execution data lacks parent-child relationships, normalized categories, and proper nesting depth. Different providers (Claude, Gemini, Codex) emit different event type names that must be mapped to a unified category system. The builder must construct timeline hierarchies for both single-turn views (hooks within one prompt-response cycle) and session-level views (turns as parents containing their hooks).

Private helper methods for grouping executions by turn, calculating nesting depth, and sorting by start time
Parent-child relationship construction based on temporal containment (child starts after parent and ends before parent)
Depth calculation ensuring children have depth = parent.depth + 1
Time range validation rejecting executions with nil startedAt

ViewModel layer for observing timeline state (covered in T003)

assumptions: HookTimelineEvent model from T001-A001 is implemented and available for import
HookExecution model exists with startedAt (Date?), completedAt (Date?), hookType (String), outcome (HookOutcome), and hookName (String) properties
EngineType enum exists with cases claude, gemini, codex for provider identification
Turn boundaries can be derived from UserPromptSubmit and Stop events in Claude, or equivalent in other providers
Maximum practical turn count per session is under 1000 for performance assumptions
Hook executions arrive with monotonically increasing startedAt timestamps within a session
constraints: Must be a value type (struct) with only static methods for stateless, testable design
Must not retain references to HookExecution or HookStore (pure transformation)
Must handle empty execution arrays gracefully returning empty result arrays
Must handle executions with nil startedAt by filtering them out (not crashing)
Must handle executions with nil completedAt (still running) by leaving endTime nil in result
Maximum depth enforced at 10 levels to prevent runaway recursion
Provider event mapping must be extensible for future providers without breaking existing logic
Time complexity should be O(n log n) or better where n is execution count
functional_requirements: FR1: HookTimelineBuilder shall be a struct with no stored properties and only static methods
FR2: buildTurnTimeline shall accept (executions: [HookExecution], turnStart: Date, turnEnd: Date?) and return [HookTimelineEvent] representing hooks within that turn boundary
FR3: buildSessionTimeline shall accept (executions: [HookExecution], turns: [TurnBoundary]) and return [HookTimelineEvent] with TurnBoundary events as parents and hooks as children
FR4: normalizeEventType shall accept (rawType: String, provider: EngineType) and return HookTimelineCategory mapping provider event names to unified categories
FR5: Builder shall filter out HookExecution objects where startedAt is nil and log a warning
FR6: Builder shall calculate depth based on temporal containment: if child.startTime >= parent.startTime and (child.endTime <= parent.endTime or parent.endTime is nil), child depth = parent.depth + 1
FR7: Builder shall sort output events by startTime ascending within each depth level
FR8: Builder shall map HookExecution.outcome to HookTimelineStatus (success -> completed, failure -> failed, etc.)
FR9: Builder shall limit maximum depth to 10 and flatten any deeper events to depth 10 with warning log
FR10: normalizeEventType shall return .tool as default for unknown event types
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: buildTurnTimeline shall process 100 executions in under 10 milliseconds on M1 hardware
NFR2: buildSessionTimeline shall process 1000 executions across 50 turns in under 100 milliseconds
NFR3: Memory allocation during build shall not exceed 2x the output array size
NFR4: Builder methods shall be thread-safe (no shared mutable state)
NFR5: All public methods shall have documentation comments describing parameters and return values
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create new file HookTimelineBuilder.swift in Blaze/Sources/Core/HookTimeline/ directory
Step 2: Define TurnBoundary struct with properties: id (UUID with default UUID()), turnNumber (Int), startTime (Date), endTime (Date?), promptPreview (String?)
Step 3: Add Identifiable conformance to TurnBoundary
Step 4: Define HookTimelineBuilder struct as empty struct (no stored properties)
Step 5: Implement private static helper filterValidExecutions(_ executions: [HookExecution]) -> [HookExecution] that removes entries with nil startedAt
Step 6: Implement private static helper sortByStartTime(_ executions: [HookExecution]) -> [HookExecution] using sorted(by:) on startedAt
Step 7: Implement private static helper mapOutcomeToStatus(_ outcome: HookOutcome) -> HookTimelineStatus with switch mapping success->completed, failure->failed, timeout->failed, pending->running
Step 8: Implement static func normalizeEventType(rawType: String, provider: EngineType) -> HookTimelineCategory with switch on provider then rawType pattern matching
Step 9: Add Claude event mappings in normalizeEventType: PreToolUse/PostToolUse -> .tool, UserPromptSubmit/Stop -> .turn, SessionStart/PreCompact -> .session
Step 10: Add Gemini event mappings: tool_call_start/tool_call_end -> .tool, prompt_start/response_end -> .turn, session_init -> .session
Step 11: Add Codex event mappings: exec_start/exec_complete -> .tool, sandbox_enter/sandbox_exit -> .session
Step 12: Add default case in normalizeEventType returning .tool with debug log for unknown types
Step 13: Implement private static helper buildHierarchy(from executions: [HookExecution], depth: Int, parentStart: Date, parentEnd: Date?) -> [HookTimelineEvent] using recursive temporal containment
Step 14: In buildHierarchy, cap depth at 10 and log warning if exceeded

Step 15: Implement static func buildTurnTimeline(executions: [HookExecution], turnStart: Date, turnEnd: Date?) -> [HookTimelineEvent] calling filterValidExecutions, sortByStartTime, then buildHierarchy with depth 0

Step 16: Implement static func buildSessionTimeline(executions: [HookExecution], turns: [TurnBoundary]) -> [HookTimelineEvent] creating parent events for each TurnBoundary and calling buildTurnTimeline for children
Step 17: Add documentation comments to all public types and methods
Step 18: Write unit tests covering all public methods and edge cases

edge_cases: Edge case 1: Empty executions array - returns empty HookTimelineEvent array without error
Edge case 2: All executions have nil startedAt - returns empty array after filtering, logs warning for each filtered execution
Edge case 3: Single execution with nil completedAt (still running) - returns single event with endTime nil and status .running
Edge case 4: Deeply nested executions exceeding depth 10 - flattens to depth 10 and logs warning message
Edge case 5: Executions with overlapping time ranges but no clear parent-child relationship - placed at same depth level sorted by startTime
Edge case 6: TurnBoundary array is empty in buildSessionTimeline - returns empty array (no parent events to attach hooks to)
Edge case 7: Execution startTime is after turnEnd - excluded from turn timeline (out of bounds)
Edge case 8: Unknown provider event type string - mapped to .tool category as fallback with debug log
Edge case 9: Clock skew causing endTime before startTime - event created with negative duration (display layer handles)
Edge case 10: Very large execution array (10000+ items) - performance may degrade but should not crash
failure_modes: FM1: HookExecution.startedAt force unwrap crash - prevented by filterValidExecutions removing nil entries before processing
FM2: Infinite recursion in buildHierarchy - prevented by depth cap at 10 levels
FM3: Memory exhaustion from large arrays - mitigated by streaming/lazy evaluation in future if needed, current design accepts 2x memory overhead
FM4: Race condition if HookExecution array mutated during build - prevented by accepting array by value (copy semantics)
FM5: Provider enum mismatch causing wrong event mapping - normalizeEventType has catch-all default case returning .tool
rollback_plan: Delete Blaze/Sources/Core/HookTimeline/HookTimelineBuilder.swift file. No database migrations or external dependencies. T001-A001 (HookTimelineEvent) remains functional independently. No UI changes to revert.

risks: Risk 1: Temporal containment logic may produce incorrect hierarchies for overlapping but non-nested executions
Risk 2: Large execution arrays may cause performance degradation beyond acceptable limits
Risk 3: Provider event mapping may become stale as CLI tools evolve their event schemas
Risk 4: Depth limiting may hide important nested information from users
mitigations: Mitigation 1: Add explicit documentation and unit tests for edge cases; overlapping non-nested executions stay at same depth level
Mitigation 2: Performance tests establish baseline; if exceeded, implement lazy evaluation or pagination in ViewModel layer
Mitigation 3: Use switch with default case returning safe fallback; log unknown types for future mapping additions
Mitigation 4: Cap at depth 10 is generous; log warning when triggered so users can report if legitimate deep nesting exists
